The subgroup-reflection problem is formalized unconditionally. An injective vertex map induces an injective map of symmetric doubles exactly when it reflects membership in the amalgamated subgroup, and injectivity on the vertex groups alone does not suffice. The canonical map of a group into its maximal group C-star algebra does reflect every subgroup and therefore induces an injective map of symmetric doubles. The cited MF permanence theorem remains partial because the repository has not proved that an arbitrary operator-MF group admits a faithful maximal-group-C-star realization in a norm matrix corona, or another MF realization to which Shulman's C-star amalgam theorem applies. The new maximal-C-star reflection theorem closes the group-theoretic bridge; the remaining issue is the analytic MF realization.
